properties.name: Ajanta, Maharashtra
properties.description: Ajanta preserves some of India’s finest surviving ancient murals depicting Jataka tales and courtly life.
properties.context: Created across multiple phases (c. 2nd century BCE to 6th century CE), these murals shaped visual storytelling across Buddhist networks.

properties.name: Ellora, Maharashtra
properties.description: Ellora demonstrates monumental rock-cut architecture and sculpture across Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain traditions.
properties.context: Between c. 6th and 10th centuries CE, Ellora became a major syncretic site of patronage and artistic experimentation.

properties.name: Delhi
properties.description: Delhi served as an imperial center where Persianate and Indic visual traditions merged in Mughal ateliers.
properties.context: From the 16th century onward, court workshops established refined narrative conventions in miniature painting.

properties.name: Jaipur, Rajasthan
properties.description: Rajput courts fostered vibrant miniature styles with devotional, literary, and musical themes.
properties.context: Regional workshops in Rajasthan evolved distinctive palettes, figuration, and court iconography between the 17th and 19th centuries.

properties.name: Kangra, Himachal Pradesh
properties.description: Kangra painting is known for lyrical landscapes and romantic-devotional narratives.
properties.context: By the 18th century, Pahari courts developed a refined style emphasizing emotional subtlety and nature.

properties.name: Kolkata, West Bengal
properties.description: Kolkata was central to nationalist-era artistic reform and the emergence of the Bengal School.
properties.context: In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, artists developed alternatives to academic realism tied to anti-colonial thought.

properties.name: Santiniketan, West Bengal
artworks: Kala Bhavana mural and sculpture traditions
properties.description: Santiniketan became a key pedagogic and experimental center connecting art, craft, and environment.
properties.context: Its curriculum emphasized contextual modernism and materially rooted practices in the early-to-mid 20th century.

properties.name: Vadodara, Gujarat
artworks: Narrative modernist works from Baroda School
properties.description: Vadodara’s Faculty of Fine Arts became a major post-independence hub for critical modernist practice.
properties.context: From the 1950s onward, artists in Baroda shaped plural, narrative approaches to modern Indian art.

properties.name: Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu
properties.description: Thanjavur is associated with richly ornamented devotional paintings and temple-centered visual culture.
properties.context: Developed under Nayaka and Maratha patronage, Tanjore painting integrated ritual use with courtly craft traditions.

properties.name: Kochi, Kerala
artists: Multiple international and Indian contemporary artists
properties.description: Kochi is a major contemporary art node through biennale-led public and site-specific practices.
properties.context: Since 2012, the Kochi-Muziris Biennale has expanded transnational dialogue in South Asian contemporary art.
